20.0 RISKS AND QUESTIONS FOR ANALYSIS

20.1 Risks

No.RiskLikelihood / effectMitigation in this design
K-1The rebuild takes long enough that V1 and V2 drift, and the owner maintains two programs.High / highCheckpoints each usable on their own; V1 frozen except fixes; regression copies tie the two; cut-over only at CP-8.
K-2The kernel's abstraction (paths, connectors) does not fit some of the owner's playful objects, and they lose what made them interesting.Medium / highFeature lists agreed per object before rewriting (FR-6.3.9); playpen scripts stay as scripts; Circular Parabola (Multi) and Linked Circles named as tests of the kernel.
K-3Readability is lost to generality: a kernel of many small parts is harder to follow than V1's one-file-per-object.Medium / highDR-2.5, DR-5.5, DR-17.3; a generator fits on a screen; kernel parts are named for what they draw.
K-4Evaluation is too slow for dragging large figures without a framework's tricks.Medium / mediumPer-layer memoisation (DR-6.6), workers (DR-16.5), budgets (DR-16.4); measured from CP-1.
K-5Snapshot undo uses too much memory on large figures.Low / mediumStructural sharing; limits in DR-7.2.
K-6Feature names (tips, intersections) renumber unexpectedly, and discs jump.Medium / high for templatesAngle numbering (DR-4.9); tracking with a 5 px rule and a "lost" state (13.7, DR-6.3); rule-based definitions later (DR-13.5).
K-7The iframe host breaks scripts that reach into the page in ways the survey missed.Medium / lowThe ledger (DR-9.7); preview-only and blocked are legitimate outcomes.
K-8An AI assistant building V2 repeats past failures: deleting unrelated code, shortcutting existing patterns.High / highThe removed-code check on every commit; layer import check; the owner's review per branch; this document as the pattern to follow.
K-9Learn leaks work or invites unreviewed changes.Low / mediumDR-14.8 to 14.10.
K-10True-scale output is wrong on a particular printer.Medium / highCalibration line on every print (DR-10.5); SVG for a known-good path.

20.2 Questions for analysts

The owner would most value an outside view on these. Each names the sections it concerns.

No.QuestionSections
Q-1Is "paths, shapers, connectors, finders" the right kernel? What common string-art constructions would it express badly?4, 13
Q-2Is a weld as a shared point number, with attachments as one-way references, sufficient, or will the owner need two-way constraints (a point on two curves at once)?6
Q-3Is whole-document snapshot undo adequate at the stated scale, or should commands record inverse operations?7
Q-4Can per-layer memoisation and workers meet DR-17.1 in plain JavaScript, or is a different drawing approach (WebGL, OffscreenCanvas) needed for large figures?6.2, 16.3, 17
Q-5Is the iframe host the right isolation for legacy scripts, versus a Worker with a canvas proxy, given that 88 scripts paint with a bare context?9
Q-6Is "folders are the truth" with small metadata files robust on Windows with VS Code editing the same files (watcher reliability, partial writes, case-insensitive names)?8
Q-7How should feature names stay stable as shapes change? Is angle numbering plus tracking enough, or is a different identity (topological, by construction) needed?4.7, 13.7
Q-8Is the regression design (geometry fingerprints, picture fallback, accept per item) the right balance of strictness and noise?16.1
Q-9What does the design make hard that the owner will probably want next (3D boards, plotters, image to thread, layered mounting)?10, 13.8
Q-10Where is the design over-built for one person's hobby tool, and what could be dropped without loss?all
Q-11Is the checkpoint order right? Would a different order give the owner something usable sooner?19
Q-12Readability: does any part of this design force code the owner will find hard to read, and is there a plainer way?2.3, 5, 17

20.3 What an analyst should not need to settle

The open items of FS 12 (O-1 to O-16) are the owner's decisions: names, sizes, colours, retention, which AI service. An analyst may comment, but the design is written to work with any answer.
